answers.ESG (v2):
## Short Answer

The iOS app crashes on the checkout screen due to a **memory leak** — memory builds up steadily the longer a user stays on that screen, eventually causing a crash. The current leading suspect, per informal investigation, is that the **SDK's image cache is not releasing thumbnails properly**. This has not yet been formally confirmed or root-caused — the investigation was still in progress ("Investigating" status, no Jira ticket filed) at the time these sources were captured.

## Supporting Evidence

**INC1122** (servicenow, status: Investigating) is the incident tracking this issue: "iOS app crashing on checkout screen for subset of users." The description notes that crash logs point to **memory pressure building up over the course of a session rather than a single bad input** — i.e., this looks like a gradual leak, not a discrete triggering bug. At the time of this record, the **mobile team** was investigating informally and had not yet filed a formal Jira story.

**slack:mobile-eng-2026-08-05** provides the technical follow-up from that informal investigation. **Sam Okafor** spent an afternoon profiling the iOS app near checkout and found that **memory climbs steadily the longer a user sits on the checkout screen** — consistent with INC1122's description. Sam's working theory is that the **SDK's image cache is not releasing thumbnails properly**, causing the leak. Sam also connected this to a related-but-unconfirmed report of the app "freezing" that other users had mentioned, describing it as "the same shape of problem" (i.e., possibly caused by the same leak).

Importantly, Sam explicitly asked for **more time to confirm the leak is actually in the SDK's cache and not something the mobile team's own code is doing wrong** before filing anything formally. This means the SDK-cache explanation is a hypothesis under active verification, not a confirmed root cause.

## What's Missing

The graph does not contain:
- Confirmation of whether the leak was ultimately traced to the SDK or to the mobile team's own code.
- Any follow-up ticket, PR, or fix once/if Sam's investigation concluded.
- Details on the "app freezing" reports Sam referenced, or whether that issue was confirmed to share the same cause.
- Any data on which "subset of users" is affected or why.

Given the frontier is exhausted, the most defensible conclusion is: the crash is caused by a memory leak that intensifies with time spent on the checkout screen, suspected (but not yet confirmed) to originate in the SDK's image/thumbnail cache.
